mechanism_narrative: Sequential improvement in TRANSIT (-47.0 to -41.4) and WORKPLACES (-39.9 to -21.0) across the last two weekly means marks resumed commuting; because retail footfall in this metro tracks commuting volume, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean of -15.7.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days is at or below -15.7 even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved week-on-week in at least two of the last three observations.

mechanism_narrative: The t-1w RETAIL_REC trough of -19.6 coincided with a PARKS spike to +6.0 and is a timing artifact of the Easter and school-holiday fortnight rather than lost demand; once the holiday distortion clears the next four weekly means revert above the last four.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the two weeks after the decision point stays below -15.7 while PARKS remains at or above -20, showing the dip was demand loss and not holiday timing.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline (+7.6 in t-1w, +6.3 in t-0w) while every other category oscillates, signalling a durable home-anchored routine that diverts spending away from discretionary store visits; the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays below the last.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds -15.7 while RESIDENTIAL weekly means remain at or above +5 in three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM falling from +2.4 to -3.6 shows households de-stocking rather than provisioning, and WORKPLACES rising from -39.9 to -21.0 shows office re-entry; together they release pantry budget and weekday footfall into discretionary categories, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean at or below 0 while WORKPLACES rises at least 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: In windows where GROCERY_PHARM is at or below 0 and WORKPLACES improves at least 10 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean in most instances.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT breaching -45 (t-1w = -47.0) marks a residual-movement-restriction regime; conditional on that crossing the mobility system is still constrained and retail footfall decays further, so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the last.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the week immediately following any observation where the TRANSIT weekly mean sits below -45.

mechanism_narrative: Reopening in this metro is sequenced so that transit capacity and office-attendance guidance loosen before retail density caps; with no active stay-at-home order, TRANSIT recovery transmits into store traffic with a two-to-four week lag and RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds the last.
regime_hint: post-lockdown reopening with no active stay-at-home orders
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is at or below -15.7 despite TRANSIT weekly means improving in at least two consecutive weeks after the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS swinging from +6.0 to -32.1 between t-1w and t-0w, a 38-point week-on-week move, marks the abrupt end of the Easter school holiday; the following fortnight is a spending void in which holiday outlays are not repeated, keeping the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change more negative than -30 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds -15.7 in any window entered after a PARKS week-on-week fall steeper than 30 points.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime that imposes density caps, WORKPLACES below -30 and RESIDENTIAL above +6 co-move as households retreat simultaneously; retail-and-recreation is the first category curtailed, so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean falls below the last.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean below -30 together with RESIDENTIAL weekly mean above +6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is at or above -15.7 in any window where WORKPLACES is below -30 and RESIDENTIAL is above +6.
